request.system: You are a sceptical results reviewer. Task: rank Medicare providers for audit. Each of 5,410 providers carries a PotentialFraud label (9.35% flagged) whose origin is undocumented; treat it as suspicion, not confirmed fraud. Claims run 27 Nov 2008 to 31 Dec 2009. The primary metric is PR-AUC; the audit queue holds about 100 providers. Pick the configuration to carry forward. Prefer a simpler model unless a more complex one is better by more than one standard deviation of PR-AUC across folds. Flag any result that looks too good. You may request up to 1 more round(s) of experiments; set stop=true if further search is unlikely to help. (Independent run 1, no feature agent.)

concerns: Run 1 (lightgbm, all) leads logistic run 3 by 0.042 PR-AUC, which is below one fold SD (about 0.057-0.068), so the simpler model is preferred under the stated rule.
Fold SDs of 0.06-0.075 are large relative to differences between configurations, so most of the ranking is within noise. The test set is small with about 506 positives, and the folds are few.

ROC-AUC of about 0.94 and PR-AUC of about 0.7 at 9% prevalence is high for a label of unknown origin. The label may be rule-derived or leaked, for example from claim volume or duplication features, so the model may reproduce the labelling rule rather than find fraud.

Size features (13 of 63) add little: no_size is roughly equal across models and within noise. Size is a proxy for provider volume and is likely to drive audit yield, so no_size is safer against volume confounding.
Precision at k=50 is 0.75-0.78 across all models, and the differences are tiny. Nothing was measured at k=100, which is the actual queue size.
Claims span only about 13 months, so there is no temporal holdout. Provider-level CV may leak through shared physicians or patients, and the results may not generalize to future periods.
Imbalance handling has little effect (run 1 and 6 use none and do as well as class_weight), so SMOTE is not worth trying.
Logistic with all features at C=0.1 has the lowest SD (0.057) and is the simplest, so carry it forward. A further round of tuning is unlikely to exceed the noise.
